_meta.purpose: Exact-token map from Wazuh alert fields to cve.now technology slugs.
_meta.policy: Match only whole field values. A group token that merely resembles a product name (mysql_login_fail, nginx_error, docker_drop) is not a technology statement and stays unmapped. A prefixed token (nextjs_probe) is added only when the token and the rule description both name the product.
_meta.validation_level: Ruleset definitions from the deployed 600-699 namespace plus the stock PHP rules shipped in the same directory. No production Indexer telemetry exists in this environment, so no mapping here is production-verified.
_meta.not_verified_against_production: No live Indexer is reachable from this workspace and none may be contacted. Run `python scripts/cve_now_tech_map_audit.py --days 30 --json` from an environment with authorized Indexer access and reconcile the report before treating tech-based correlation as production-verified.

audit.command: export WAZUH_INDEXER_URL=... WAZUH_INDEXER_USER=... WAZUH_INDEXER_PASSWORD=... WAZUH_INDEXER_VERIFY_SSL=true; python scripts/cve_now_tech_map_audit.py --days 30 --json > cve-now-audit.json
audit.requests: POST {index}/_search with size:0 and a GET {index}/_field_caps probe. No document bodies, no writes, no script or pipeline clause.

buckets.confirmed: token is in this map and was observed
buckets.in_map_not_observed: token is in this map and did not appear in the window
buckets.unmapped_needs_review: a whole segment of the group name equals a slug; a human decides
buckets.unmapped_log_source_only: only the decoder or log path names the slug; this is where the log was written, not what the rule is about

audit.rule: A group is added only when the name itself names a technology and the sampled rules are about that product. Log source alone never justifies a mapping, and a production hit never raises correlation confidence: tech matches stay `candidate`.
audit.status: not run: no Indexer in this environment

evidence.observed: Descriptions name WordPress: access pattern, wp-login.php brute force, XML-RPC brute force, directory listing.
Descriptions say 'Next.js internal path access', 'Multiple Next.js internal path accesses'.
CVE-2025-55182 exploitation rules; descriptions name 'React Server Component/Next.js Server Action' and 'Next.js Server Action'.
Description: 'RCE Payload Detection (React2Shell/Next.js): Command Execution dalam Request Body/Data'.
Descriptions: 'Encoded PHP script injection attempt via GET', 'PHP webshell upload/execution attempt via POST'.
Same PHP injection and webshell-upload detections.

ambiguous_kept_unmapped.react2shell: Carried alone on 621009/621010 (Turbopack/Webpack dev endpoints) and beside nextjs on 621006-621008. It names an exploit family that covers React Server Components and Next.js, which are separate cve.now slugs, so picking one would be a guess.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.mysql_login_fail: 612015 lives in 612-mariadb_rules.xml and describes a 'MySQL failed login attempt'. The group says MySQL, the file says MariaDB, and cve.now has both slugs. Either mapping would guess which product the deployment runs.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.windows_iis: 604121 names Windows IIS explicitly, but cve.now has no IIS slug, so there is no supported target. Mapping it to microsoft-exchange would be wrong.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.linux: 604079-604081 are webshell detections that carry an OS tag. linux-kernel is a kernel slug; an OS tag is not a kernel claim.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.php2shell: A webshell payload class, not a PHP version or product.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.payload_obfuscation: 621005 matches obfuscated JS bodies; no product is named.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.nginx_error: An event-type token, and it appears only in a local draft (php2shell/wazuh-rulesnya/existing_rules_old.xml), not in the deployed ruleset.
ambiguous_kept_unmapped.nextjs_action: Appears only in vuln-research/wazuh-nextjs-react2shell-rules.xml, which is not part of the deployed 600-699 ruleset.
